speaker: Miss Cheryl Chan Wei Ling
text: MSO was established to improve the Government's overall coordination and delivery of municipal services.

speaker: Miss Cheryl Chan Wei Ling
text: In my past speeches, I noted that residents have been using OneService App actively and commended on its ease of use and good response by the agencies.

speaker: Miss Cheryl Chan Wei Ling
text: What were the nature of some issues that have been resolved in the past from such co-creation and are there any areas that could further be improved in order to allow more communities to benefit from them through best practice sharing?

speaker: Miss Cheryl Chan Wei Ling
text: Of course, communal living brings along with it some inherent challenges and a need for much tolerance and civic mindedness of the general public.

speaker: Miss Cheryl Chan Wei Ling
text: I know my Pioneer Group Constituency (GPC) colleagues and I have been repeating this in this House several times, including what you have just heard from the earlier cuts.

speaker: Miss Cheryl Chan Wei Ling
text: MND and the Ministry of Sustainability and the Environment (MSE) have repeatedly responded about the past effort and how regulations alone have limitations in tackling the issues resolutely.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: I will speak on housing and our efforts to transform the built environment sector.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: My colleague, Minister Indranee Rajah, will cover our long-term planning, sustainable development, and our support for our construction firms.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: Senior Minister of State Sim Ann will touch on how we are working alongside residents and our community partners to improve our living environment.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: Senior Minister of State Tan Kiat How will share about our efforts to transform Singapore into a City in Nature.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: HDB started selling subsidised flats to Singaporeans in 1964 under the Home Ownership Scheme.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: Today, 80% of our people live in HDB homes, of whom 90% own their homes.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: During our Forward Singapore engagements, Singaporeans told us clearly that homeownership remains a key aspiration.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: So, we will honour this commitment and ensure that there are housing options for every budget and need.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: Members will recall the significant impact that COVID-19 had on our construction sector as well as on our housing market.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: There were unprecedented supply disruptions and labour shortages, causing widespread delays.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: This resulted in an imbalance in demand and supply, pushing up housing prices and rents.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: Application rates for new HDB flats rose to a peak.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: We are well on track to meeting our 2025 target.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: We have also ramped up private housing supply.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: In 2023 alone, we launched 9,250 units under the Government Land Sales, or GLS, scheme.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: This was the highest annual supply in the last 10 years.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: And for the first half of this year, 2024, we released land for 5,450 private homes on the Confirmed List.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: This is the highest supply on the Confirmed List in a single GLS Programme in over 10 years.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: We are watching the market carefully and are prepared to inject even more housing supply if necessary to meet demand.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: Across the public and private housing markets, a significant number of new homes have been completed.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: This is the largest number in a single year since 2018.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: In parallel, we implemented three rounds of cooling measures since December 2021 to moderate housing demand, and to encourage greater financial prudence among homebuyers.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: HDB resale prices rose 4.9% last year, less than half of the 10.4% increase the year before, in 2022.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: Price growth in the private residential market has also moderated, from 8.6% in 2022 down to 6.8% in 2023.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: BTO application rates went down, from a high of 5.8 applications per flat in 2020 to 2.9 applications per flat last year.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: Transaction volume in the private property market in 2023 declined by 13% compared to 2022 and is at its lowest since 2016.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: The quarterly increase in public housing rents moderated to 0.4% in the fourth quarter of last year, down from 1.9% in the third quarter of last year.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: Private housing rents fell by 2.1% quarter-over-quarter in the fourth quarter of 2023.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: This was the first quarterly decline in over three years.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: We expect the housing market to continue to stabilise this year.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: We will continue to launch a steady supply of new homes in various locations, so that there is a home for every budget and need.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: Amidst persisting economic uncertainties, geopolitical tensions and higher interest rates, we encourage buyers to be prudent in their home purchases to avoid over-extending themselves.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: Miss Cheryl Chan asked how we will plan to address growing near-term needs.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: We are developing greenfield sites and brownfield areas, some of which have potential heritage significance.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: In doing so, we take great care to retain our identity and collective social memories.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: If we foresee major impact on sites with significant heritage, we will carry out studies in consultation with key stakeholders.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: We also pay attention to the environmental impact of these developments and carry out studies to minimise such impact.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: So far, we have announced our plans to build new housing in various locations, including in more central parts of Singapore, such as Pearl's Hill, Mount Pleasant, Bukit Timah Turf City and the former Keppel Golf course.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: Today, I would like to share our plans for another two areas.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: With its development as a new housing area, we will provide more new homes and amenities in Yishun.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: We will build a variety of recreational, community and commercial facilities to bring greater convenience to residents, while adding vibrancy to Yishun Town.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: These will complement existing facilities at Khatib Central and HomeTeam NS Khatib.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: This will provide a sizeable supply of new homes, particularly for those who wish to live near their parents in the area.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: The second area we are developing plans for is Gillman Barracks in Telok Blangah.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: Gillman Barracks has a storied history and is home to former colonial military buildings.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: Besides providing more opportunities for Singaporeans to live closer to the city centre, the new residential neighbourhood can build on the character and charm of the former colonial buildings.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: These will help us better understand the ecological and heritage significance of the site and to plan sensitively for its development.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: As always, we will share our plans with Singaporeans, and hear your feedback and suggestions.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: My colleague, Minister Indranee, will elaborate on our efforts later.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: We have been announcing new housing sites at a steady clip.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: This is underpinned by our long-term approach towards land use and infrastructure planning.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: In doing so, we adopt various long-term strategies to optimise and steward our limited land.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: For example, we are studying major moves like the development of Long Island to tackle rising sea levels while creating new land and opportunities.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: We are also freeing up land for redevelopment, such as through the relocation of Paya Lebar Airbase.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: At the heart of these plans is the Government's commitment that public housing remains affordable, inclusive and fair for all Singaporeans and that Singapore remains a vibrant city, an endearing community and a cherished home for all of us.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: Beyond developing a steady supply of homes, we have also made major changes to our public housing system to ensure that it remains affordable and accessible for Singaporeans.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: These improvements were made after consulting thousands of Singaporeans as part of Forward Singapore.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: First, as we build more flats in more central locations, we want to ensure that public housing remains affordable for more Singaporeans.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: Mr Henry Kwek asked how we will ensure that Plus and Prime housing remain affordable and inclusive.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: We will provide additional discounts and subsidies for these flats, as well as grants such as the means-tested Enhanced CPF Housing Grant (EHG).

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: Mr Xie Yao Quan asked about how we will enhance housing options for singles.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: With the launch of the new HDB framework, singles will be able to buy new 2-room Flexi flats islandwide, Plus, Prime and Standard.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: We received many other ideas during our Housing Conversations too.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: We will continue to review our housing policies to support the aspirations of singles and other groups of Singaporeans.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: For parents and married couples who are trying to secure their very first home to settle down, we implemented the First-Timer (Parents and Married Couples) priority category, in October of last year.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: This increases the chances of success for eligible married couples and parents in securing their first home from HDB, as they seek to start their families.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: Mr Xie Yao Quan asked about the projected demand from this group.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: We are still monitoring the application and success rates since it only came into effect late last year.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: But so far, I am glad to see that many families have benefited.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: Across our BTO launches in October and December last year, about nine in 10 First-Timer (Parents and Married Couples) applicants were issued a queue number within the flat supply available.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: For home buyers in the resale market, we increased the quantum of the CPF Housing Grant last year, to support First-Timers.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: We will continue to review our grants, paying particular attention to supporting our low-income households.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: This year, we will make two further moves to support Singaporeans’ housing needs.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: First, we want to help young couples to settle down earlier, if they are ready to do so as a couple.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: In our Forward Singapore Housing Conversations, many young couples appreciated the support to help them buy their homes.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: This includes the EHG, as well as our efforts to ramp up Shorter Waiting Time flats, and of course, the First-Timer (Parents and Married Couples) priority scheme.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: But some still face financial difficulties in booking a flat, particularly those who are still studying or in National Service (NS).

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: As Mr Henry Kwek mentioned, there are also some young homebuyers who need to support their parents when they start work and find it hard to build up their savings.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: These young couples do not qualify for the EHG, which requires 12 months of continuous employment, as they have not yet started working or have only just started working.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: Furthermore, these couples are likely to face difficulties in qualifying for a sizeable housing loan at the point in time of application.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: Today, we have various measures to help these young couples, who are full-time students or full-time national servicemen (NSFs), or who have completed their full-time studies or NS in just the past year.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: As they are circulating the handouts, let me just share that first, we allow such couples to book a new flat, while they defer their income assessment for the EHG and an HDB housing loan to shortly before they collect their keys.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: At this later date, they are more likely to be eligible for the EHG as well as a larger HDB loan.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: We also extend the Staggered Downpayment Scheme (SDS) to these couples.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: They only need to pay half of the initial downpayment required for their new HDB flat, with the balance paid at the point of key collection.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: For those taking an HDB housing loan, they pay 5% of the flat price, instead of 10%.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: While those taking a loan from financial institutions pay 10% of the flat price, instead of 20%.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: I am glad that many young couples have benefited from these measures.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: We want to do more to help lighten the initial financial burden for such young couples.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: Since they have deferred their income assessment, they will only receive their EHG closer to key collection, and must rely on their own savings or support from family for initial costs of booking a flat.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: For some of them, the reduced 5% initial downpayment under the SDS is still a significant financial barrier.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: This will apply whether they take an HDB housing loan or a loan from a financial institution.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: So, this means that those who take an HDB loans, from 5%, now 2.5%.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: For those taking loans from banks, from 10% to 2.5%.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: To illustrate, let us look at the pamphlet in front of you.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: A young couple who is taking an HDB loan to buy a 4-room BTO flat in Bedok, a Mature Estate.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: They are tapping on the deferred income assessment as one of them is a full-time student and the other is a full-time NSman.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: Suppose the flat is priced at $480,000 before grants.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: Today, should they tap on the SDS, the 5% initial downpayment is $24,000.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: With our enhancement to the SDS, this will be further reduced to $12,000, which is more affordable for them.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: For couples who are ready to purchase a flat and have been saving up to afford the downpayment, we hope that this enhancement will help you to settle down and start your families earlier.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: Ms Hazel Poa had suggested other ways to support our families and to tackle our nation’s declining TFR.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: We have addressed them previously in this House.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: Ms Hazel Poa suggested increasing the number of Shorter Waiting Time Flats launched in our BTO exercises.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: As we have mentioned before, we had started planning for more flats with shorter waiting times of three years or less before the COVID-19 pandemic.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: These are flats that are built a year or more before they are launched.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: But we had to bring forward their launch dates to meet the immediate demand during the pandemic, to tide through the challenging period.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: We are now ramping up on Shorter Waiting Time flats again.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: As I said earlier, we launched our very first Shorter Waiting Time flat back in 2018.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: This was affected by COVID-19, and now we are getting back on track.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: We will continue to recalibrate our building programme over time so that Shorter Waiting Time flats make up a larger proportion of new flat supply.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: In fact, waiting times of recent launches have generally come down too.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: The median waiting time for projects launched in 2023 was three years and 10 months.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: At the recent BTO sales exercise in February, more than 80% of the BTO flats launched have a waiting time of three and a half years or less.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: Next, on expanding singles’ access to public housing.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: The PSP is proposing to allow singles to access public housing from 28 years old, and to buy 3-room flats.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: Many other Members of Parliament from both sides of the House have made similar suggestions, one time or the other.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: We are working hard to ramp up our flat supply in order to meet the anticipated increase in demand from this move.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: In fact, as I have explained previously in this house, if we had all the land and resources at this point in time to further expand singles’ access even further, or for that matter, expand access to other groups of Singaporeans, we would already have done so.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: But we also have to meet growing demand from married couples, from families, from seniors and many other groups of Singaporeans.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: If we were to adopt Ms Poa's suggestions now without being able to increase our flat supply correspondingly, BTO application rates will spike and resale prices will soar.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: Many people who want flats will not be able to get them, including the singles whom she is trying to help.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: This would be counter-productive to the PSP’s objective of supporting TFR.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: When young couples and families cannot get flats, it would make it even harder for them to settle down.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: Our approach has instead been to design our public housing policies carefully to address the needs of every segment, while ensuring the stability and sustainability of our system.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: We are living, after all, in a small island city-state.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: For Singaporeans who plan to get married, please rest assured that we have a slew of support measures to help you settle down quickly, including priority access to BTO flats as an First-Timer (Parents and Married Couples) applicant.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: The enhanced SDS that we have just announced is another measure that will help you book a flat and settle down earlier.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: These are families who have booked a flat, but need temporary accommodation while awaiting the completion of their flat.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: Today, we provide subsidised temporary housing for these families under the PPHS.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: Mr Louis Ng and Ms Nadia Samdin have asked for updates on the PPHS.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: We have also refined the PPHS eligibility conditions and allocation process to prioritise families in greater need.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: As a result, we have been able to better meet demand from eligible families.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: Meanwhile, as Deputy Prime Minister Wong has announced in the Budget speech, we will introduce a PPHS (Open Market) Voucher for one year until our PPHS supply is ramped up to 4,000 units next year, to support eligible families who need to rent HDB flats or bedrooms on the open market.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: Mr Murali Pillai noted the need to minimise distortion of the rental market.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: That is why we have scoped the parameters of the voucher carefully, to support these families while minimising the potential impact on the broader rental market.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: This voucher will be available to families who meet the PPHS eligibility criteria.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: Broadly, these are Singaporean families with a household income of $7,000 or less, who are waiting for their HDB flats to be completed.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: This allows us to target the PPHS Voucher at those with less income at their disposal, to defray their costs of renting.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: Payment will be made on a reimbursement basis.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: Some may ask, why not a higher amount?

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: The $300 quantum was carefully calibrated to provide some relief to eligible families, while mitigating the potential inflationary impact on the rental market for others.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: At $300 per month, eligible families will receive up to $3,600 if they qualify for the full year of support.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: Mr Louis Chua has proposed to expand HDB’s rental programme, and Mr Leong Mun Wai too.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: Just last year, the PSP introduced the Millennial Apartments Scheme and shared that it was a way to build small, rental flats in prime locations near the central business district for younger Singaporeans to rent for a period of time.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: Today, they expand this scheme, I understand, to mature estates as well as to replace future Prime and Plus flats with Millennial Apartments instead.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: This means taking back Mature Estate land and land in more central parts of Singapore with currently owner-occupied flats, and instead of building Prime and Plus flats with the concomitant restrictions to support owner-occupation, for people to buy.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: This means, under their scheme, replacing them with large numbers of rental flats for young millennials to rent out for a few years.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: This, of course, in an island city state with limited land, will mean very significant trade-offs, and fewer supply for many other groups of Singaporeans, including those that will have to be displaced as a result of the redevelopment plans of the PSP.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: In fact, today we already have a range of rental and co-living options in both the HDB market, as well as in the private market, as well as HDB programmes such as the Public Rental Flat Scheme, Interim Rental Housing, PPHS.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: As I have said earlier, we will continue to study ideas shared with us during the Forward Singapore Housing Conversations, including the ideas that Members of this House have raised and continue to study how to enhance further the housing option diversity in Singapore.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: But as I have shared earlier, the vast majority of Singaporeans still aspire to own a home, if not now, then eventually.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: This was reaffirmed at our Forward Singapore engagements with over 21,000 Singaporeans.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: And so, we are prioritising our resources to help Singaporeans achieve homeownership.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: This has always been our position, even as we seek to provide more diversity and choice in our market and a safety net for those who are not yet ready to buy their own homes.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: This is a continuous work in progress and I thank Members from both sides of the House for your good ideas.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: In fact, this will continue to be our commitment to Singaporeans.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: As our society ages, it is important that we transform our homes and estates to better support our seniors.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: At the estate level, we will upgrade our precincts to make them safer and easier for our seniors to move around in.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: We will also provide more precinct amenities, where our seniors can stay active and bond with other residents.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: At the flat level, we will introduce more enhancements through EASE 2.0, so that they feel safe and comfortable at home.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: My HDB colleagues have been working hard on the implementation details for these plans and some of these details are now ready.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: Senior Minister of State Sim Ann and Minister of State Faishal Ibrahim will touch on them later.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: Mr Chairman, Mr Chong Kee Hiong and Assoc Prof Jamus Lim have also asked about VERS.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: Assoc Prof Lim focused on the mechanics of the scheme and the impact on home owners, specifically making a suggestion for lower voting thresholds for older flats.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: While Mr Chong Kee Hiong also spoke about the wider context of urban rejuvenation and redevelopment.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: Indeed, VERS should be seen as part of a bigger strategy for us to comprehensively plan for the redevelopment of our public housing, improve the environment and quality of life in our heartlands, create towns that further embrace “live-work-play” strategies, and bring jobs and amenities closer to our people.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: It involves re-imagining all over again, the concept of public housing and reinvigorating our ageing HDB towns.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: In doing so, we have to take care of the current generation’s housing needs even as we cater for the needs of future generations.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: We will need to carefully stage redevelopment in the older parts of the towns, while minimising disamenities to the residents in the newer parts.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: Some Singaporeans will need to relocate as a result of this, so we will need to work through the detailed mechanics and processes and the package for VERS.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: We will also need to ensure that there are sufficient homes available at the right time for them.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: We are developing these details and plans and will announce more information and details in due course.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: We have taken care of Singaporeans’ housing needs for the past 60 years.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: We will continue to do so for the next 60 years and beyond.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: I will now turn to our built environment sector.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: Through our refreshed Industry Transformation Map (ITM), we have been helping our construction firms to digitalise, raise their productivity, and build more sustainably.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: So far, we have made good progress in digitalising the sector by encouraging the adoption of Integrated Digital Delivery (IDD).

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: IDD connects different stakeholders in a building project via a “digital spine”.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: Examples include the adoption of virtual environments to simulate real-world construction.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: We have also shifted towards more productive ways of building, by raising the adoption of Design for Manufacturing and Assembly (DfMA) technologies.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: This enables the off-site prefabrication of building components in a safer, more productive, factory-like setting before they are shipped to the worksite and assembled.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: Over the years, we have made moves to push for DfMA as the default method of construction in Singapore.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: For instance, it is a requirement for all developments on land sold under the GLS programme.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: We also enhanced the Buildability Framework in 2022 so that all large building projects of at least 25,000 square metres must adopt DfMA.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: We are similarly on track to meet our target of 70% DfMA adoption by 2025.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: Minister Indranee Rajah will share more about our progress towards a more sustainable built environment sector.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: We must continue to push the envelope, to ensure that our construction industry is well-poised for further transformation.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: To do this, we will enhance the Building and Construction Authority's (BCA’s) Contractors Registration System (CRS).

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: Currently, firms that are bidding for public sector construction tenders need to be registered under the CRS.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: The CRS is also one of three gateways for firms to access foreign construction workers.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: The other two gateways are: BCA’s Builders Licensing Scheme (BLS), and the Singapore List of Trade Sub-contractors (SLOTS), which is managed by the Singapore Contractors Association Ltd (SCAL).

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: Today, the entry requirements to CRS, BLS and SLOTS are uneven.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: This means that some firms may find it easier to access foreign construction workers under certain gateways.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: While we recognise the need for foreign construction workers in the sector, the firms that are allowed to hire them should meet the same minimum standards.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: This means that CRS will expand its reach.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: It will shift from being a public sector registry, to a nation-wide registry of construction firms.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: With this nation-wide registry in place, we can raise and harmonise quality, manpower and productivity, and innovation standards more effectively, across the entire construction industry.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: We will do so progressively, to mitigate the impact to firms as well as to construction projects.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: BCA will announce further details of the changes, including the implementation timeline, later this year.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: BCA has engaged key industry stakeholders, and they understand the impetus for these changes.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: Minister Indranee will share more details on other upcoming initiatives to support firms in their transformation journey.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: (In Mandarin):   This year marks the 60th anniversary of HDB's Home Ownership Scheme.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: Over the past 60 years, the Government has been committed to providing public housing for Singaporeans and supporting their dream of home ownership.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: We understand that Singaporeans have been concerned about the housing market in recent years.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: Some parents worry that their children may not be able to afford housing and some young couples are eager to receive their keys to start a family.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: Through various Government measures, the housing market has recently began to stabilise.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: The rate of increase of housing prices and rent is easing and the application rate for BTO flats has also decreased.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: I believe that in the coming year, the situation will become more stable.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: As the housing needs of Singaporeans evolve, our housing policies must also evolve in tandem, to allow Singaporeans to afford and own their own homes.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: It was earlier announced that starting from the second half of this year, we will implement a new public housing classification framework to ensure that public housing remains affordable.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: They will be able to purchase new 2-room flats in any area.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: We have also introduced a new First-Time (Parents and Married Couples) BTO applicant category to help eligible families secure a HDB flat as soon as possible.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: This year, we will provide more assistance to help young couples own their own homes.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: We know that for young Singaporeans who are still studying or serving NS, or those who have just graduated and finished NS, having to pay the downpayment of their flat when they have not entered the workforce can be financially challenging.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: Currently, they can pay for the flat downpayment in phases.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: They will first pay one portion when they sign the Agreement for Lease.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: The remaining will only have to be paid when they collect their keys.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: Of course, we have also not forgotten the seniors.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: The Government will continue to rejuvenate HDB estates and neighbourhoods to provide a safer and more liveable living environment for the elderly, helping them to age in place and to enjoy their golden years.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: We are also working hard on the preparations for VERS.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: Through VERS, we can redevelop the land comprehensively, better integrate elements of "live, work and play" into our towns and bring more employment opportunities and amenities to HDB estates.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: However, redeveloping HDB estates is a very complex task.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: As we redevelop ageing towns, we need to carefully balance the housing needs of future generations as well as consider those of the current generation.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: We will generally need to redevelop the older parts of a town in stages and minimise the inconvenience to other residents.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: This also means that some people will need to relocate and we need to ensure that there will be enough housing units for them to move to.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: Due to its large scale and complexity, VERS will be an important project that will span several decades.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: We will ensure that every aspect of VERS is properly planned and will announce more details at an appropriate time. : Mr Chairman, providing good homes, planning for our land use and transforming our built environment sector – these are important areas that we must continue to forge ahead.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: The collective efforts of Singaporeans and our stakeholders: planners, construction firms, community groups and so on, have helped to shape our nation and make Singapore a distinctive city.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: We will continue to work with Singaporeans to build an inclusive, sustainable, and vibrant home for generations to come.

speaker: The Second Minister for National Development (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: Mr Chairman, a small island-state, that is our nation, has thrived against all odds.

speaker: The Second Minister for National Development (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: With 734 square kilometres of land, we have been able to build homes for a nation and a globally vibrant economy, with a world-class airport and seaport, while protecting our greenery and our built heritage.

speaker: The Second Minister for National Development (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: Through careful stewardship and deliberate long-term planning, we have been able to make the most of our limited land and continue to provide a quality living environment for Singaporeans.

speaker: The Second Minister for National Development (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: We have benefited from the foresight of our pioneer planners, who envisioned what we could become.

speaker: The Second Minister for National Development (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: Careful stewardship and deliberate, long-term planning will continue to guide how we plan our land use to balance current needs and those of future generations.

speaker: The Second Minister for National Development (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: We are working closely with Singaporeans to shape our urban and built environment.

speaker: The Second Minister for National Development (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: First, having engaged Singaporeans on our Long-Term Plan Review, we will now engage Singaporeans on our Draft Master Plan; second, we will develop sustainably and sensitively; and third, we will support our built environment firms in their transformation journey.

speaker: The Second Minister for National Development (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: We are now embarking on the Master Plan Review which translates these long-term strategies into implementable plans over the next 10 to 15 years.

speaker: The Second Minister for National Development (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: Miss Cheryl Chan and Mr Chong Kee Hiong asked how the Government intends to involve Singaporeans in the Master Plan review.

speaker: The Second Minister for National Development (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: Through our engagements, we will hear about Singaporeans' hopes and dreams for our city and see how we can make them a reality while working within our constraints.

speaker: The Second Minister for National Development (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: We will be engaging the public on significant plans for parts of Singapore.

speaker: The Second Minister for National Development (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: This includes protecting the low-lying East Coast area from sea level rise, strengthening our flood resilience and water supply, building new homes and creating new coastal and reservoir parks.

speaker: The Second Minister for National Development (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: Ms Nadia Ahmad Samdin asked about the impact of "Long Island" on marine life.

speaker: The Second Minister for National Development (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: Today, agencies are already required to conduct detailed environmental studies for developments that may cause significant environmental impact and develop appropriate mitigating measures. "Long Island" will be no different.

speaker: The Second Minister for National Development (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: The studies for "Long Island" will consider surrounding marine habitats, such as intertidal flats and coral communities.

speaker: The Second Minister for National Development (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: We will work closely with the nature community, academics and researchers to explore nature-based solutions to minimise the environmental impact of the reclamation of "Long Island".

speaker: The Second Minister for National Development (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: Senior Minister of State Tan will cover other aspects of how we conserve and plan our marine spaces.

speaker: The Second Minister for National Development (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: We have commenced discussions with some stakeholders and will progressively do so with others, including recreational interest groups, businesses, the local community and the general public.

speaker: The Second Minister for National Development (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: These conversations, together with findings from technical studies, will guide the development of a shared vision for "Long Island".

speaker: The Second Minister for National Development (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: We will also be engaging the public on our islandwide planning strategies.

speaker: The Second Minister for National Development (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: For example, "Play" was one of the themes of the Long-Term Plan Review where many Singaporeans shared their desire for more recreational opportunities.

speaker: The Second Minister for National Development (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: To follow up, URA and agencies are developing a Recreation Master Plan.

speaker: The Second Minister for National Development (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: As part of the Recreation Master Plan, we are working to activate and curate networks of recreational spaces across the island, incorporating sports, arts, nature, heritage and wellness.

speaker: The Second Minister for National Development (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: These spaces will help keep Singapore liveable, amidst our densely built-up environment, something Mr Dennis Tan spoke about.

speaker: The Second Minister for National Development (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: These recreation spaces will be both indoor and outdoor, close to homes and well-connected via footpaths, cycling paths and park connectors.

speaker: The Second Minister for National Development (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: Between the second quarter and third quarter this year, URA will hold a series of roving exhibitions across the island to seek the public's views on the planning of recreation spaces.

speaker: The Second Minister for National Development (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: The feedback received here will then feed into the Draft Master Plan.

speaker: The Second Minister for National Development (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: Through our engagements, we will reach out to a wide spectrum of stakeholders, including youths, interest groups, local communities, academics and industry partners.

speaker: The Second Minister for National Development (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: Plans will be showcased at the exhibition for public feedback, before it is gazetted as the next Master Plan.

speaker: The Second Minister for National Development (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: Beyond our Draft Master Plan engagements, we are continually committed to work with Singaporeans in the planning and designing of our spaces.

speaker: The Second Minister for National Development (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: This includes ways to facilitate safe and efficient deliveries, as shared by Ms Jean See, which we will study further.

speaker: The Second Minister for National Development (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: We hope that through these conversations, we can all have a better understanding of the diverse needs and aspirations among Singaporeans and how to meet these, given our land limitations and emerging challenges, like climate change.

speaker: The Second Minister for National Development (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: Even as we develop for the future, we aim to do so sensitively and sustainably.

speaker: The Second Minister for National Development (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: This is a key concern that many Singaporeans had raised in our past engagements.

speaker: The Second Minister for National Development (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: We continue to adopt creative solutions and new technologies to protect our island against the impact of climate change.

speaker: The Second Minister for National Development (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: Mr Dennis Tan asked how we are keeping Singapore liveable amidst rising temperatures and whether population density is considered in our planning norms.

speaker: The Second Minister for National Development (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: Key factors that drive the urban heat island, or UHI effect, are building density and the types of human activity, rather than population density.

speaker: The Second Minister for National Development (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: For example, while Central Business District (CBD) and industrial areas have lower population density, they are temperature hotspots.

speaker: The Second Minister for National Development (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: To minimise the UHI effect, we have implemented a wide suite of cooling strategies, at various scales across the landscape.

speaker: The Second Minister for National Development (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: At the national level, greening Singapore remains a key strategy that brings many benefits, including providing shade, cooling our surroundings and enhancing our living environment.

speaker: The Second Minister for National Development (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: Senior Minister of State Tan will share more about our City in Nature efforts.

speaker: The Second Minister for National Development (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: At the development and district level, we configure new towns and districts to optimise wind flow and ventilation, as well as to reduce heat gain from the sun.

speaker: The Second Minister for National Development (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: At the building-level, we are trialling cool coatings which reflect heat-generating radiation back to the atmosphere.

speaker: The Second Minister for National Development (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: On climate mitigation, Mr Xie Yao Quan asked what efforts we have taken to accelerate our transformation to a low-carbon built environment.

speaker: The Second Minister for National Development (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: The MEI regime is targeted at energy-intensive buildings.

speaker: The Second Minister for National Development (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: Building owners of such buildings will be required to conduct an energy audit and implement measures to reduce energy consumption.

speaker: The Second Minister for National Development (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: We are also doing more to green the construction process.

speaker: The Second Minister for National Development (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: As mentioned in the Deputy Prime Minister's Budget speech and Senior Minister of State Low Yen Ling's Ministry of Trade and Industry (MTI) COS speech, we will be expanding the Energy Efficiency Grant, or EEG, to new sectors, including construction.

speaker: The Second Minister for National Development (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: This is a new grant for the construction industry and will support the cost of energy-efficient construction equipment.

speaker: The Second Minister for National Development (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: Under the Advanced Tier, firms that wish to do even more to reduce their emissions can receive funding support of up to S$350,000, inclusive of the support under the Base Tier.

speaker: The Second Minister for National Development (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: This advanced tier will allow firms to adopt energy-efficient equipment that is not pre-approved.

speaker: The Second Minister for National Development (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: The grant amount for this will be based on expected energy savings or up to 70% of the equipment cost, whichever is lower.

speaker: The Second Minister for National Development (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: We target to introduce the EEG for the construction industry by the end of this year.

speaker: The Second Minister for National Development (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: Beyond driving greater sustainability, we must continue to transform the built environment sector in other ways.

speaker: The Second Minister for National Development (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: Miss Cheryl Chan asked about our efforts to encourage the adoption of productive and innovative technologies in the built environment.

speaker: The Second Minister for National Development (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: We have developed a system of incentives and grants to support investments in different types of technologies.

speaker: The Second Minister for National Development (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: For example, the Productivity Solutions Grant has helped over 900 construction and facilities management SMEs adopt pre-approved digital solutions to date.

speaker: The Second Minister for National Development (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: We will also extend the Productivity Innovation Project, or PIP, scheme until March 2025.

speaker: The Second Minister for National Development (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: The scheme provides our builders and prefabricators with co-funding support of up to 70% of the costs of technologies, such as robotics and automation, capped at S$10 million.

speaker: The Second Minister for National Development (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: Over the last six years, the PIP scheme has supported 78 firms with S$37.4 million worth of funding in investments.

speaker: The Second Minister for National Development (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: For example, Great Resources M&E Contractor Pte Ltd will be deploying automated drilling and anchoring robots onsite.

speaker: The Second Minister for National Development (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: This will enable the firm to increase productivity by at least 30%, with one-third less workers required.

speaker: The Second Minister for National Development (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: With less manual work and fewer workers onsite, they can also carry out this work more safely.

speaker: The Second Minister for National Development (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: I encourage firms to make use of the PIP extension to transform their processes.

speaker: The Second Minister for National Development (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: The system of incentives I have just mentioned is targeted at helping individual firms transform their work.

speaker: The Second Minister for National Development (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: However, building projects involve many different parties across the broader built environment value chain.

speaker: The Second Minister for National Development (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: To encourage collaboration, we introduced the Growth and Transformation Scheme, or GTS, which supports alliances of developers, builders, consultants and other stakeholders to pursue best-in-class transformation outcomes together.

speaker: The Second Minister for National Development (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: As of January 2024, both the CapitaLand Development-led and City Developments Limited-led alliances have started to implement their initiatives.

speaker: The Second Minister for National Development (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: For example, CapitaLand Development's upcoming Common Data Environment platform will facilitate upfront coordination and structured information exchange throughout the project.

speaker: The Second Minister for National Development (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: It will be the single reference point for key project information.

speaker: The Second Minister for National Development (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: I commend CapitaLand Development and its alliance partners, including Woh Hup, Surbana Jurong and Threesixty Consultants, for their efforts and look forward to hearing more about their progress.

speaker: The Second Minister for National Development (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: I also thank Mr Henry Kwek, Mr Don Wee and Mr Yip Hon Weng for their suggestions on how to better support our construction firms.

speaker: The Second Minister for National Development (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: Firms can tap on many existing incentives to grow their capabilities.

speaker: The Second Minister for National Development (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: These include the sector-specific initiatives I spoke about and other broader schemes.

speaker: The Second Minister for National Development (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: The Government also does our part as a major buyer of construction services.

speaker: The Second Minister for National Development (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: For example, agencies are required to abide by strict timeframes so that firms receive payments on time.

speaker: The Second Minister for National Development (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: This includes regular milestone payments and partial payments when Variation Orders are progressively completed.

speaker: The Second Minister for National Development (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: Every stakeholder is critical in this journey, from our residents and nature and heritage groups, to our professional bodies and built environment firms.

speaker: The Second Minister for National Development (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: I urge each of you to actively participate in our stakeholder engagements, share your insights and contribute to the conversation that will shape Singapore.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Ms Sim Ann)
text: Mr Chairman, I thank Members for their cuts.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Ms Sim Ann)
text: Building a quality living environment continues to be a priority for MND.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Ms Sim Ann)
text: We proactively upgrade and revitalise our neighbourhoods, housing estates and flats, in line with the evolving needs, lifestyles and aspirations of Singaporeans, We will do more, together with our public and private sector partners, in three areas.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Ms Sim Ann)
text: Second, ensuring that neighbourhoods have a range of affordable and accessible amenities and shops.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Ms Sim Ann)
text: First, let me share how we are upgrading our towns and flats.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Ms Sim Ann)
text: To better support ageing-in place, MND, MOH and Ministry of Transport announced a set of initiatives under Age Well SG last November.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Ms Sim Ann)
text: These include physical upgrading to enhance our neighbourhoods and flats to be more senior-friendly.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Ms Sim Ann)
text: Under this new phase, we will build more senior-friendly amenities, such as therapeutic gardens with wheelchair-friendly planter boxes, fitness trails connecting senior-centric amenities and wayfinding features.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Ms Sim Ann)
text: These amenities enhance the safety and connectivity of our neighbourhoods while helping seniors stay active and navigate confidently around their neighbourhoods.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Ms Sim Ann)
text: Some older precincts have already undergone upgrading and do not qualify for NRP.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Ms Sim Ann)
text: We announced last November that HDB will roll out similar senior-friendly enhancements to more than 20 of such precincts in the towns of Ang Mo Kio, Bukit Merah, Queenstown and Toa Payoh over the next five years.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Ms Sim Ann)
text: The roll-out of these silver upgrading works will be progressive, starting with a pilot in Ang Mo Kio.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Ms Sim Ann)
text: To Mr Henry Kwek's question, HDB will engage Town Councils, the grassroots and residents on the implementation of these works.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Ms Sim Ann)
text: HDB will share more with Town Councils when ready.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Ms Sim Ann)
text: In fact, they are designed from the start to be age-inclusive to encourage inter-generational bonding, a topic brought up by Ms Nadia Samdin.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Ms Sim Ann)
text: For example, HDB has introduced 3-Generation or 3G recreation spaces, with fitness corners and playgrounds placed side by side.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Ms Sim Ann)
text: Such playgrounds enable residents of different age groups to interact with one another.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Ms Sim Ann)
text: We also co-locate childcare and elderly facilities where possible.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Ms Sim Ann)
text: To Mr Lim Biow Chuan's question, I would like to assure Members that there are inspection regimes in place today to detect and rectify building deterioration in a timely manner.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Ms Sim Ann)
text: The Building Control Act requires regular building inspections by professionals.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Ms Sim Ann)
text: These include checks for spalling concrete and structural cracks, for both common areas and within the flat.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Ms Sim Ann)
text: In the longer term, every flat will be upgraded twice, the first when they are about 30 years old, through the Home Improvement Programme, or HIP; and the second, through HIP II, when they are about 60 to 70 years old.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Ms Sim Ann)
text: When undergoing HIP, flats will undergo repairs for spalling concrete and structural cracks, which HDB fully subsidises.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Ms Sim Ann)
text: HIP II will be offered when the first batch of flats reach their 60- to 70-year mark.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Ms Sim Ann)
text: HDB is currently working out the prioritisation and implementation details.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Ms Sim Ann)
text: To Mr Pritam Singh's question on the challenges and delays in implementing upgrading works, various factors may contribute to delays, including unforeseen site conditions, manpower availability, cashflow issues and disruptions in supply of materials.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Ms Sim Ann)
text: For projects managed by HDB, HDB will work with the relevant contractor to understand the causes for the delays and render the appropriate assistance to get the project back on track.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Ms Sim Ann)
text: If the contractor can no longer fulfil its obligations, it may novate the contract to another firm, subject to HDB's approval.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Ms Sim Ann)
text: As a last resort, HDB can also exercise its right to terminate the contract and appoint another firm to complete the project.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Ms Sim Ann)
text: Another challenge that we face is rising costs.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Ms Sim Ann)
text: To Mr Ang Wei Neng’s question, we have been reviewing and adjusting programme budgets, taking into consideration prevailing macroeconomic conditions and changes in tender price indices.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Ms Sim Ann)
text: For example, in 2022, we increased the NRP budget by $850 per flat for then-ongoing NRP projects, in response to the impact of COVID-19.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Ms Sim Ann)
text: With the continued increase in costs, we are prepared to further increase the NRP budget.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Ms Sim Ann)
text: We will inform Town Councils of details when ready.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Ms Sim Ann)
text: We have also been flexible, acceding to ad-hoc appeals for additional budget due to increases in material and manpower costs.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Ms Sim Ann)
text: First, on Mr Dennis Tan and Mr Ang Wei Neng's questions on the Lift Upgrading Programme, or the LUP.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Ms Sim Ann)
text: LUP has brought direct lift access to around 5,000 blocks and today, around 99% of all HDB blocks were either built with direct lift access or have benefitted from LUP.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Ms Sim Ann)
text: Members will recall that many of these blocks were built when our population was a lot younger and when physical mobility was not an issue.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Ms Sim Ann)
text: Because same floor lift access was not required as a condition of design, there were some blocks that were designed in such a way that the retrospective adding of lift shafts and lifts is technically very difficult or even unfeasible.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Ms Sim Ann)
text: What HDB has been doing is to trial new technology and to apply new methods wherever possible.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Ms Sim Ann)
text: So, this has included, in the past, using machine-room-less lifts as well as the use of smaller home lifts to bring lift upgrading to blocks that previously were very difficult for us to add lifts to.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Ms Sim Ann)
text: However, although we have worked hard to shrink the pool of blocks that cannot undergo LUP over the years, there remain some blocks where LUP is currently not feasible due to cost or technical constraints.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Ms Sim Ann)
text: Mr Dennis Tan has made points on consulting ground feedback for LUP.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Ms Sim Ann)
text: I wish to clarify that HDB values the inputs of Town Councils when it comes to LUP works because HDB recognises that it is the Town Councils that will have to maintain the lifts when built.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Ms Sim Ann)
text: In the case of Aljunied-Hougang Town Council, it was involved in the LUP Working Committee formed for block 833, Hougang Central which I believe is in the Mr Dennis Tan's ward.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Ms Sim Ann)
text: In addition, HDB does take into account ground concerns from residents who might not be part of the benefiting units but feel affected by lift upgrading solutions or from the MPs whom they might approach.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Ms Sim Ann)
text: Usually, these concerns can be resolved, for example, by the addition of privacy fins.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Ms Sim Ann)
text: The current minimum contribution rates for Town Councils' LRF and Sinking Funds help Town Councils set aside sufficient funds for various cyclical replacement works.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Ms Sim Ann)
text: The restricted use of these funds serves as a form of fiscal discipline.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Ms Sim Ann)
text: Lift replacements are very infrequent but involve heavy draw-down of funds when they are due, as lifts built in the same period will need to be replaced around the same time.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Ms Sim Ann)
text: Hence, the LRF allows Town Councils to pay for any capital expenditure relating to lift replacements in HDB estates, including those raised by Mr Gerald Giam.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Ms Sim Ann)
text: We will continue to review the framework periodically to ensure that they keep pace with changes to the operating context.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Ms Sim Ann)
text: HDB towns are designed to give all residents convenient access to amenities and shops, often within 400 metres of their homes.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Ms Sim Ann)
text: At the heart of every HDB town is a Town Centre, a key commercial hub providing a wide range of goods and services.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Ms Sim Ann)
text: We also have Neighbourhood Centres and precinct shops distributed across the town.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Ms Sim Ann)
text: HDB also imposes trade mix controls to ensure that residents' basic needs are met.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Ms Sim Ann)
text: For town and neighbourhood centres, HDB allows for greater market flexibility as the larger number of shops provides sufficient opportunity for market forces to determine a good trade mix.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Ms Sim Ann)
text: HDB adopts the Price-Quality Method (PQM) tender mechanism to attract quality retailers whereby HDB considers factors other than tender bid prices, such as affordability, business concepts and community-centric initiatives.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Ms Sim Ann)
text: To further enhance the vibrancy of our commercial precincts, we will be trialling the refreshment of commercial clusters through placemaking and trade curation at three pilot sites – Ang Mo Kio Town Centre, Bukit Gombak and Tampines West Neighbourhood Centres.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Ms Sim Ann)
text: As shared by my co-chair in the Heartland Digitalisation and Revitalisation Committee, Minister of State Low Yen Ling, this will be done in collaboration with MTI and Enterprise Singapore (ESG).

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Ms Sim Ann)
text: Our HDB and Town Council colleagues, alongside local stakeholders, will also be supporting MTI and ESG's Heartland Enterprise Placemaking Grant for heartland enterprises keen to champion ground-up placemaking events.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Ms Sim Ann)
text: HDB is also working on developing trade mix plans for these pilot sites together with residents, merchants and other stakeholders.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Ms Sim Ann)
text: Last year, I shared about our budget meals initiative in HDB-owned coffee shops.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Ms Sim Ann)
text: We have made good progress and I thank Mr Murali Pillai for tracking this initiative and giving his views on how we can improve it.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Ms Sim Ann)
text: More than 130 coffee shops rented from HDB are already offering budget meals and drinks.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Ms Sim Ann)
text: More will come onboard as their tenancies are progressively renewed.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Ms Sim Ann)
text: To the point that Assoc Prof Jamus Lim has made, I wish to clarify that for HDB coffee shops let out via PQM tender, we require at least six stalls to provide one budget meal each alongside two budget drinks.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Ms Sim Ann)
text: And for renewals of HDB-owned coffee shops that are rented out, we require four budget meals and two budget drinks.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Ms Sim Ann)
text: This ensures a range of food and drink options at affordable prices.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Ms Sim Ann)
text: In a related move, we launched BudgetMealGoWhere last year, an online platform that helps the public find coffee shops offering budget meals and drinks.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Ms Sim Ann)
text: With the help of GovTech, we also launched the Great Budget Meal Hunt in January this year, where the public can share their recommendations of affordable meals.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Ms Sim Ann)
text: Since its soft launch in October last year, we have added over 290 user-submitted budget meals and drinks to the platform.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Ms Sim Ann)
text: We have received more than 1,900 recommendations and 2,800 verifications of budget meals from the public, which will be progressively added to the BudgetMealGoWhere portal.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Ms Sim Ann)
text: We will study whether to extend these conditions further.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Ms Sim Ann)
text: Next, l will share how we intend to work with the community to co-create solutions to deal with municipal issues in our estates.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Ms Sim Ann)
text: More than 200,000 Singaporeans participated in the Forward Singapore exercise.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Ms Sim Ann)
text: When I sat in for some of these conversations, I was encouraged that many Singaporeans care about forging pro-social norms in the community and have concrete ideas on how to go about it.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Ms Sim Ann)
text: At the same time, as Miss Cheryl Chan has pointed out, the Municipal Services Office (MSO) is celebrating its 10th anniversary this year.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Ms Sim Ann)
text: MSO has come a long way from our early days, focused on improving coordination of service delivery among the now 10 Government agencies and 17 Town Councils.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Ms Sim Ann)
text: Going forward, we will do more to deepen engagement with residents and community partners.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Ms Sim Ann)
text: We strongly encourage community partners to share their ideas and work with us to create norms which help us keep our living environment harmonious and well-maintained.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Ms Sim Ann)
text: Through our various pilots, we are also developing new operating models that we can adopt to improve our response to municipal issues.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Ms Sim Ann)
text: First, we will continue to leverage technology for convenient municipal feedback reporting by observant residents.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Ms Sim Ann)
text: Feedback providers can now use a range of digital channels, including the OneService app and LifeSG; or interact with Kaki, the OneService Chatbot, on familiar platforms like WhatsApp, Telegram and Instagram.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Ms Sim Ann)
text: Later this year, residents can look forward to giving feedback by providing only photos and location of the issue to Kaki, making it even more convenient to provide feedback on-the-go.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Ms Sim Ann)
text: Second, we want to empower residents by lowering barriers for residents to initiate community action.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Ms Sim Ann)
text: MSO will continue to avail resources, advice and small-scale funding for residents to start their own projects that encourage pro-social norms.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Ms Sim Ann)
text: For example, through our Love Our 'Hood co-creation projects, residents can develop and refine their ideas in workshops and subsequently implement them in their neighbourhoods.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Ms Sim Ann)
text: Residents can also seek funding by tapping onto MSO's Love Our 'Hood Fund.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Ms Sim Ann)
text: To date, 13 projects have received such support and we encourage residents with good ideas to apply.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Ms Sim Ann)
text: Alongside such community engagements, MSO will continue to pioneer new operating models that improve the Government's response to municipal issues.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Ms Sim Ann)
text: First, we have taken decisive steps to address a persistent pain point for feedback providers.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Ms Sim Ann)
text: Today, agencies occasionally close straightforward feedback cases ahead of the works being completed as their KPIs are weighted towards the speed of reply.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Ms Sim Ann)
text: Such cases include requests for cleaning, local infrastructure maintenance and vector control.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Ms Sim Ann)
text: We applied this requirement to a small subset of agency-owned OneService cases in 2020 and by the end of the year, this will be required of all straightforward agency-owned OneService cases.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Ms Sim Ann)
text: Second, we have reorganised the delivery of 10 common municipal services in Tampines.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Ms Sim Ann)
text: These common municipal services are now delivered by a single operator instead of individual agency contractors.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Ms Sim Ann)
text: It no longer matters "which agency's issue" it is, as service delivery will be seamless to residents.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Ms Sim Ann)
text: This is complemented by worker cross-training, empowering a combined team with operations technology and rewarding efforts to address municipal issues thoroughly, address root causes of recurrent issues and undertake preventive maintenance and repair.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Ms Sim Ann)
text: In our next phase of experimentation, we have expanded this to Pasir Ris-Punggol to see if we can achieve similar efficiencies over a larger area.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Ms Sim Ann)
text: If it continues to produce good results, we will scale this to more estates.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Ms Sim Ann)
text: Last year, MCCY, MinLaw and MSO shared our multi-pronged, community-led approach to tackling neighbour noise disputes.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Ms Sim Ann)
text: Complementing this, MSO has set up an initial team of dedicated personnel, on a pilot basis, who will leverage stronger laws and technology to investigate and enforce against the small number of severe neighbour noise disputes.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Ms Sim Ann)
text: As Members may have heard in Second Minister Edwin Tong's MinLaw Committee of Supply speech, we will also be enhancing the mediation framework and the Community Disputes Resolution Tribunals (CDRT) process.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Ms Sim Ann)
text: For example, the mediation framework will be adjusted to resolve more neighbourhood disputes at an earlier stage, including through mandatory mediation.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Ms Sim Ann)
text: The public expressed broad support for stronger Government intervention in these severe cases during consultations in 2023.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Ms Sim Ann)
text: (In Mandarin):   Starting from last year, the Government has gradually introduced a budget meal plan in the coffee shops owned by HDB.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Ms Sim Ann)
text: We will explore ways to encourage more operators to sell budget meals.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Ms Sim Ann)
text: Many residents who have used the app find it convenient and easy to use.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Ms Sim Ann)
text: However, some users occasionally observe that although the relevant authorities have responded saying they will address their feedback, the issues have not been thoroughly resolved.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Ms Sim Ann)
text: MSO has gradually worked with the relevant Government agencies to raise the requirements, for them to treat residents' feedback more rigorously.
