speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Ms Sim Ann)
text: As long as the issues reported by users are straightforward, Government agencies cannot simply instruct contractors to address the issues and then respond to users.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Ms Sim Ann)
text: They must confirm that the work has been successfully completed before closing the case and providing a response; and if possible, include photos to demonstrate that the issue has been properly resolved. : Chairman, back to English.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Ms Sim Ann)
text: I have shared on our efforts to ensure our neighbourhoods and flats continue to meet residents' evolving needs and remain vibrant, even as they age.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Ms Sim Ann)
text: Concurrently, we will also deepen partnerships with the community to co-create and co-deliver solutions, as well as adopt new operating models for municipal services delivery.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Ms Sim Ann)
text: Together, we strive to achieve improvements in Singaporeans' living environment.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Mr Tan Kiat How)
text: Mr Chairman, greening has been a national priority since Independence in 1965.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Mr Tan Kiat How)
text: In our next bound of greening, we aim to make Singapore a City in Nature.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Mr Tan Kiat How)
text: Ms Nadia Ahmad Samdin asked for updates on our progress.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Mr Tan Kiat How)
text: First, we are establishing more green spaces and enhancing existing ones.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Mr Tan Kiat How)
text: We also opened a new section of Pasir Panjang Park.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Mr Tan Kiat How)
text: This is one of the 13 parks along the Southern Ridges and West Coast that we will rejuvenate and link up with curated trails.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Mr Tan Kiat How)
text: We are also making our green spaces more accessible and inclusive.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Mr Tan Kiat How)
text: Last year, we launched five therapeutic gardens in our parks.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Mr Tan Kiat How)
text: Second, we are strengthening the connectivity between our green spaces.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Mr Tan Kiat How)
text: These efforts bring us closer to nature and strengthen our ecological resilience, by facilitating the movement of native fauna between habitats.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Mr Tan Kiat How)
text: We are also curating other island-wide recreation routes, such as the Rail Corridor, Central Corridor and Coast-to-Coast trails.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Mr Tan Kiat How)
text: Just last month, we completed the Eastern Corridor.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Mr Tan Kiat How)
text: Singaporeans can now enjoy 18 kilometres of scenic land and waterscapes, as you walk, jog or cycle from Pasir Ris Park to East Coast Park.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Mr Tan Kiat How)
text: Third, we are restoring nature into our urban fabric and safeguarding our rich biodiversity.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Mr Tan Kiat How)
text: We are close to achieving our target of 200 hectares by 2030, and we have restored and enhanced over 40 hectares of forest, coastal and marine habitats since 2020.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Mr Tan Kiat How)
text: With this, we are halfway to meet our enhanced target of 80 hectares by 2030.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Mr Tan Kiat How)
text: We have also been enhancing the Sisters' Islands Marine Park and we look forward to reopening Big Sister's Island to the public this year.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Mr Tan Kiat How)
text: Highlights will include a new coastal forest trail, tidal lagoon and specially designed subtidal biodiversity panels along the floating boardwalk.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Mr Tan Kiat How)
text: These will allow visitors to observe marine life up-close with minimal impact on the ecosystem.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Mr Tan Kiat How)
text: Mr Louis Ng mentioned a target, adopted at the 15th Conference of Parties to the UN Convention on Biological Diversity, to conserve 30% of coastal and marine areas by 2030.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Mr Tan Kiat How)
text: Like the other targets under the Kunming-Montreal Global Biodiversity Framework, this is a global rather than a national target.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Mr Tan Kiat How)
text: Countries are expected to contribute according to their national circumstances, priorities and capabilities.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Mr Tan Kiat How)
text: Singapore is contributing through our efforts under our National Biodiversity Strategy and Action Plan, taking into account our unique circumstances as a small, densely populated city-state.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Mr Tan Kiat How)
text: To Mr Ng and Ms Nadia Ahmad Samdin's question on additional marine parks, we will continue to carefully balance the different needs in planning for our sea spaces, such as recreation, shipping and aquaculture – with conservation, under the Draft Master Plan 2025.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Mr Tan Kiat How)
text: Mr Ng has also asked if we will consider enacting a new EIA law.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Mr Tan Kiat How)
text: Today, environmental considerations are already taken into account upstream in the land-use planning process.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Mr Tan Kiat How)
text: Environmental studies are required for developments, which may cause significant environmental impact, and appropriate mitigation measures will be put in place and closely monitored.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Mr Tan Kiat How)
text: We have been strengthening the EIA process over the years.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Mr Tan Kiat How)
text: For example, we have published detailed guidelines for biodiversity impact assessments and we are piloting the centralised management of EIA consultancy services under NParks.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Mr Tan Kiat How)
text: Let us monitor the effect of these changes, before we decide whether we need to take any further steps to enhance our EIA framework.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Mr Tan Kiat How)
text: Ms Nadia Ahmad Samdin has also asked how we will involve even more members of the community in our efforts.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Mr Tan Kiat How)
text: The community's support is crucial to realise our City in Nature vision.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Mr Tan Kiat How)
text: As part of the OneMillionTrees movement, more than 100,000 members of the community have joined us in planting over 640,000 trees.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Mr Tan Kiat How)
text: Under the Nature Kakis Network, 140 passionate grassroots volunteers across 16 chapters and counting have been driving ground-up initiatives.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Mr Tan Kiat How)
text: We have also nurtured around 350 youth stewards through the Youth Stewards for Nature programme since 2021.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Mr Tan Kiat How)
text: Through such efforts, NParks aims to grow its volunteer base from 48,000 to 70,000 by 2030.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Mr Tan Kiat How)
text: As a densely populated city-state, we are very mindful that we need to carefully manage human-wildlife encounters to ensure that Singaporeans feel safe in and around our green spaces.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Mr Tan Kiat How)
text: That is why we take a proactive, comprehensive and science-based approach in managing wildlife populations.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Mr Tan Kiat How)
text: We partner the nature community to engage the public on how to responsibly interact with and appreciate nature through platforms, such as school assemblies, HDB's MyNiceHome roadshows and the Nature Kakis Network.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Mr Tan Kiat How)
text: NParks adopts a range of targeted measures to manage different wildlife species, from pest birds, long-tailed macaques, otters, wild boars to crocodiles, as each species has its unique characteristics.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Mr Tan Kiat How)
text: We continually refine our approach based on ongoing research and international best practices.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Mr Tan Kiat How)
text: NParks also conducts surveillance and enforcement against the illegal feeding of wildlife, such as pest birds, which Mr Lim Biow Chuan has asked about.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Mr Tan Kiat How)
text: For example, NParks deploys CCTV cameras and enforcement personnel at known feeding hotspots.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Mr Tan Kiat How)
text: With evidence, NParks will take enforcement action against the feeder.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Mr Tan Kiat How)
text: Mr Louis Ng has asked if we will introduce a statutory presumption provision for wildlife feeding, similar to that for high-rise littering.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Mr Tan Kiat How)
text: Under NEA's presumption provision for high-rise littering, if there is clear evidence that an act of littering has been committed from a particular residential flat, the registered owners or tenants of the flat will be presumed to have committed the offence.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Mr Tan Kiat How)
text: Today, this provision can already be exercised where bird feeders throw food from high-rise windows, as such acts are considered high-rise littering.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Mr Tan Kiat How)
text: However, this provision is contingent on the ability to pinpoint the wrongdoing to a specific unit, that is registered to a specific individual or individuals.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Mr Tan Kiat How)
text: As a large majority of illegal wildlife feeding cases take place in outdoor public areas, such a provision would not be applicable.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Mr Tan Kiat How)
text: Instead, as the main challenge in such cases is obtaining clear evidence that pinpoints the wrongdoer, evidence gathering remains key.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Mr Tan Kiat How)
text: To this end, NParks will step up surveillance at identified feeding hotspots.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Mr Tan Kiat How)
text: We understand the disamenities to residents from pigeons, such as the soiling of public spaces and laundry.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Mr Tan Kiat How)
text: Tackling this issue requires a multi-pronged, multi-stakeholder effort.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Mr Tan Kiat How)
text: NParks, the Singapore Food Agency (SFA) and National Environment Agency (NEA) have been consistently supporting Town Councils on their pigeon management efforts.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Mr Tan Kiat How)
text: For example, NParks has been advising Town Councils on best practices for pigeon removal operations and has leaned forward to conduct live demonstrations.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Mr Tan Kiat How)
text: That said, we need to tackle the issue at its root, by reducing human-generated food sources in our estates.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Mr Tan Kiat How)
text: In addition to discouraging and enforcing against illegal bird feeding, agencies have been working with Town Councils to improve food waste management, such as by encouraging the prompt clearance of leftover food from food centre tables and the proper closure of bins.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Mr Tan Kiat How)
text: In the coming months, we will step up our effort for Town Councils to better manage the pigeon population, especially in certain hotspots.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Mr Tan Kiat How)
text: Some ideas we are looking at include detailed guidelines on effective pigeon removal operations and conducting site-specific assessments and interventions to reduce food sources.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Mr Tan Kiat How)
text: We are also keenly aware of the interlinkages between human and animal health.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Mr Tan Kiat How)
text: Animals can carry diseases that can be transmitted to humans and vice versa.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Mr Tan Kiat How)
text: Bio-surveillance is a crucial line of defence against zoonotic disease outbreaks.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Mr Tan Kiat How)
text: NParks has been partnering fellow One Health agencies – MOH, NEA, SFA and PUB – on a range of efforts.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Mr Tan Kiat How)
text: This includes the monitoring and analysis of animal health data and environmental indicators so that we can swiftly detect and respond to diseases, avert potential outbreaks, and safeguard both public and animal health.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Mr Tan Kiat How)
text: The programme will harness expertise and emerging technologies across multiple disciplines, such as genomics, disease modelling and vector biology, to improve our understanding of the key drivers of zoonotic disease transmission in Singapore.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Mr Tan Kiat How)
text: This will help us to develop more effective upstream mitigation strategies, including a more effective system to monitor and detect animal diseases.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Mr Tan Kiat How)
text: The research findings will also provide industry stakeholders and the wider public, including pet owners, with valuable insights on best practices for preventing zoonotic diseases.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Mr Tan Kiat How)
text: Researchers can look forward to grant calls later this year.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Mr Tan Kiat How)
text: Mr Louis Ng has asked about our approach to tackling animal cruelty.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Mr Tan Kiat How)
text: We take a serious view of all acts of animal cruelty.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Mr Tan Kiat How)
text: The Animal and Veterinary Service (AVS) investigates all feedback and will take appropriate enforcement action.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Mr Tan Kiat How)
text: We are looking at the possibility of enhancing penalties for animal cruelty. as part of our ongoing review of the Animals and Birds Act.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Mr Tan Kiat How)
text: The review spans a range of areas, from enhancing protections for animal health and welfare, to strengthening safeguards on public health and safety.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Mr Tan Kiat How)
text: As such, we will need time to formulate the proposals, and to consult the public and relevant stakeholders.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Mr Tan Kiat How)
text: We will continue to work closely with animal welfare groups to promote responsible interactions with animals, through platforms such as Pets' Day Out events, school plays and webinars.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Mr Tan Kiat How)
text: Last December, I shared our proposed cat management framework.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Mr Tan Kiat How)
text: We closed our public survey on the proposed framework last month.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Mr Tan Kiat How)
text: For example, some called for mandatory pet cat sterilisation, while others did not support this.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Mr Tan Kiat How)
text: We are studying the responses carefully and will share more details when ready.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Mr Tan Kiat How)
text: (In Mandarin):   We have made good progress towards our goal of transforming Singapore into a City in Nature.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Mr Tan Kiat How)
text: Last year, we completed Lakeside Garden within Jurong Lake Gardens.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Mr Tan Kiat How)
text: This year, we will open the revamped Chinese Garden and Japanese Garden.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Mr Tan Kiat How)
text: These efforts bring us closer to nature and strengthen our ecological resilience.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Mr Tan Kiat How)
text: At the same time, to ensure that Singaporeans can safely enjoy our green spaces, we take a proactive, comprehensive and science-based approach to managing wildlife populations.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Mr Tan Kiat How)
text: We work closely with stakeholders to promote safe and responsible human-wildlife encounters.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Mr Tan Kiat How)
text: We also recognise the interconnectedness of human and animal health.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Mr Tan Kiat How)
text: Diseases can be transmitted between animals and humans.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Mr Tan Kiat How)
text: Biosurveillance is a critical line of defence against zoonotic disease outbreaks.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Mr Tan Kiat How)
text: This programme will enhance our understanding of the key drivers of zoonotic disease transmission in Singapore and help us to develop more effective upstream mitigation strategies for our urban context. : In conclusion, in transforming Singapore into a City in Nature, partnerships are key.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Mr Tan Kiat How)
text: This will help us to better manage human-wildlife interactions and strengthen safeguards on public and animal health.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Mr Tan Kiat How)
text: We have made good progress, but there is more to be done.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Mr Tan Kiat How)
text: As we press on with our efforts, we will continue to collaborate with stakeholders and the wider community.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Mr Tan Kiat How)
text: Together, we can shape a green, vibrant and resilient Singapore that we are all proud to call home.

speaker: The Minister of State for National Development (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: Chairman, I thank Members for their views on supporting the housing needs of seniors, lower-income and vulnerable households.

speaker: The Minister of State for National Development (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: As Singapore matures and grows, we must do so inclusively and take care of the diverse and changing needs of our population.

speaker: The Minister of State for National Development (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: Today, I will focus on two key areas: first, on uplifting our lower-income households and preserving social mobility; and second, on ensuring that Singapore remains a safe and comfortable home for our ageing population.

speaker: The Minister of State for National Development (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: For lower-income households with no other housing options, public rental housing is a key social safety net.

speaker: The Minister of State for National Development (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: We recognise that shelter alone is not enough.

speaker: The Minister of State for National Development (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: For many of these families, complex and overlapping challenges, such as illness or unemployment, often get in the way.

speaker: The Minister of State for National Development (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: To address these challenges early, we pair rental housing with social support.

speaker: The Minister of State for National Development (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: These families are paired with a ComLink+ family coach soon after entry into public rental housing.

speaker: The Minister of State for National Development (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: Through early and sustained engagement with the families, ComLink+ family coaches can tailor their support to what each family needs, fostering stability, self-reliance and, ultimately, social mobility.

speaker: The Minister of State for National Development (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: When these rental households are ready, we support them in their transition towards home ownership.

speaker: The Minister of State for National Development (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: We have a range of measures in place to support both first-timer and second-timer rental households in making this transition.

speaker: The Minister of State for National Development (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: Like other first-timer Singaporean families, first-timer families in public rental can tap on the Enhanced CPF Housing Grant to receive up to $80,000 to support them in their purchase of their first home from HDB.

speaker: The Minister of State for National Development (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: For second-timer rental families, the Fresh Start Housing Scheme boosts their housing budget and supports them in regaining and sustaining home ownership.

speaker: The Minister of State for National Development (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: The Fresh Start Housing Scheme has been enhanced in the past two years to help more families.

speaker: The Minister of State for National Development (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: We increased the grant amount from $35,000 to $50,000 and gave Fresh Start families who may need a larger flat the option to purchase more affordable 3-room flats on shorter leases.

speaker: The Minister of State for National Development (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: As of end January 2024, we have 101 families who have tapped on the Fresh Start Housing Scheme to book a new flat.

speaker: The Minister of State for National Development (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: Besides the various housing schemes and grants available, HDB also has the Home Ownership Support Team, or HST in short, to provide one-to-one guidance to help rental households navigate the flat buying process.

speaker: The Minister of State for National Development (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: One family that has benefited from HST's support and the Fresh Start Housing Scheme is Mdm Hazlinda Binte Tahar and her three children.

speaker: The Minister of State for National Development (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: Keen to regain home ownership, Mdm Hazlinda reached out to HST for help in understanding her family's housing budget and options.

speaker: The Minister of State for National Development (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: In December 2023, with HST's support and help from the Tenants' Priority Scheme, Mdm Hazlinda successfully booked a 3-room Sale of Balance flat, with a shorter lease of 50 years.

speaker: The Minister of State for National Development (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: With her CPF savings and the Fresh Start Housing Grant, she was able to complete the flat purchase without a loan.

speaker: The Minister of State for National Development (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: As of end 2023, HST has engaged close to 1,600 households.

speaker: The Minister of State for National Development (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: Of these, over 120 have moved into their new homes and another close to 100 families have booked their flats and are waiting to collect their keys.

speaker: The Minister of State for National Development (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: We have also been looking into new ways to better support singles in public rental housing.

speaker: The Minister of State for National Development (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: Today, under the Joint Singles Scheme, or JSS, singles must apply for a rental flat with a flat mate.

speaker: The Minister of State for National Development (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: While most JSS tenants can find a flat mate and live together without issues, we recognise that this may be difficult for some.

speaker: The Minister of State for National Development (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: This is why we have been exploring new typologies to improve the living experience of singles living in public rental housing.

speaker: The Minister of State for National Development (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: Ms Carrie Tan, Mr Faisal Manap and Mr Louis Chua have asked for updates on these new typologies.

speaker: The Minister of State for National Development (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: The JSS Operator-Run model, or JSS-OR for short, is an ongoing pilot from December 2021.

speaker: The Minister of State for National Development (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: Under JSS-OR, singles can apply for a rental flat without a flat mate.

speaker: The Minister of State for National Development (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: A social service agency appointed by HDB operates each site, including managing the flat sharing arrangements and mediating between tenants when disagreements arise.

speaker: The Minister of State for National Development (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: Last year, we expanded the pilot to three new sites in Bukit Panjang, Bidadari and Sengkang.

speaker: The Minister of State for National Development (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: With these additional sites, HDB has assisted about 600 JSS-OR tenants as of end-2023 and can accommodate up to 1,000 tenants in total.

speaker: The Minister of State for National Development (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: One tenant that has benefited from JSS-OR is Mr Lee, who is in his 70s.

speaker: The Minister of State for National Development (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: After the friend he was living with passed away, Mr Lee had to turn to public rental housing.

speaker: The Minister of State for National Development (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: At his age and with his medical needs, Mr Lee had trouble finding a flat mate to apply with under the JSS.

speaker: The Minister of State for National Development (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: With the help of a social worker, Mr Lee applied for the JSS-OR instead.

speaker: The Minister of State for National Development (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: After he was accepted to the Bukit Panjang site, the JSS-OR operator helped to pair him with a compatible flat mate and Mr Lee moved in in October 2023.

speaker: The Minister of State for National Development (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: Since then, Mr Lee and his flat mate have been getting along well.

speaker: The Minister of State for National Development (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: As demonstrated through Mr Lee’s experience, I am happy to share that the pilot has been progressing well.

speaker: The Minister of State for National Development (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: Mr Lee and many other tenants have shared their appreciation for the on-site social service agency whom they can approach for assistance when needed.

speaker: The Minister of State for National Development (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: The model has also been effective in mitigating co-tenant conflicts.

speaker: The Minister of State for National Development (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: Over 95% of such conflicts were resolved through the on-site operators' early mediation and adjustment of flat sharing arrangements where necessary.

speaker: The Minister of State for National Development (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: Some operators have also gone the extra mile, for example, by organising activities to encourage interaction and bonding amongst tenants.

speaker: The Minister of State for National Development (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: We will further evaluate the pilot outcomes, before adjusting and expanding the model to meet the needs of the tenants and operators.

speaker: The Minister of State for National Development (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: Another pilot typology is the Single Room Shared Facilities model, or SRSF.

speaker: The Minister of State for National Development (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: Through SRSF, we aim to give singles in public rental more privacy while making good use of limited space and preventing social isolation.

speaker: The Minister of State for National Development (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: Thereafter, we look forward to housing the first batch of successful applicants from around the third quarter 2024.

speaker: The Minister of State for National Development (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: This will support our seniors who wish to age in place, in their communities.

speaker: The Minister of State for National Development (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: Miss Cheryl Chan, Ms Tin Pei Ling, Mr Henry Kwek and Ms Nadia Samdin have asked about Age Well SG, including on our efforts to support seniors with little or no family support.

speaker: The Minister of State for National Development (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: First, under Age Well SG, we had announced the expansion of the wireless Alert Alarm System, or AAS, to all seniors aged 60 and above living in public rental housing.

speaker: The Minister of State for National Development (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: The wireless AAS is an emergency button that is linked to nearby Active Ageing Centres and CareLine, a 24/7 hotline that provides response to callers in distress.

speaker: The Minister of State for National Development (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: The feedback from seniors in rental blocks that currently have the wireless AAS installed has been positive.

speaker: The Minister of State for National Development (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: Seniors found the alert system particularly helpful during emergencies.

speaker: The Minister of State for National Development (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: Last month, I visited Mr Abdul Rahim and Mdm Ernowati, an elderly couple staying in a 1-room rental flat in Jalan Besar.

speaker: The Minister of State for National Development (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: In the past year, the couple has activated the wireless AAS three times to call for help after Mr Abdul Rahim experienced breathlessness and collapsed at home.

speaker: The Minister of State for National Development (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: After activating the alert button, they were connected to CareLine staff who promptly alerted the Singapore Civil Defence Force (SCDF) to send him to the hospital.

speaker: The Minister of State for National Development (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: During my visit, both Mr Abdul Rahim and Mdm Ernowati shared that they felt more assured with the wireless AAS in their home.

speaker: The Minister of State for National Development (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: Its round-the-clock emergency response service allowed them to receive medical help promptly, especially when Mr Abdul Rahim collapsed late at night.

speaker: The Minister of State for National Development (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: We will start with rental blocks with a higher number of seniors, such as in Bukit Merah and Kallang-Whampoa.

speaker: The Minister of State for National Development (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: We hope that, as a result of this effort, our seniors in public rental will feel safer when living independently at home.

speaker: The Minister of State for National Development (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: Further, under Age Well SG, we had also announced the expansion of senior-friendly features offered under the Enhancement for Active Seniors, or EASE programme, to enhance the safety and well-being of seniors in their homes.

speaker: The Minister of State for National Development (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: The earlier announced features include rocker switches, home fire alarm devices, the widening of bathroom entrances and handrails at main entrances with steps.

speaker: The Minister of State for National Development (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: In addition to the above, we will be introducing additional features targeted at improving bathroom safety and fall prevention for seniors under EASE 2.0.

speaker: The Minister of State for National Development (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: These include lowered bathroom entrance curbs, foldable U-profile grab bars and bidet sprays.

speaker: The Minister of State for National Development (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: Bathrooms carry a significant fall risk for seniors and we hope these features will help keep our seniors safe.

speaker: The Minister of State for National Development (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: Mr Henry Kwek had asked when the EASE 2.0 roll-out would commence.

speaker: The Minister of State for National Development (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: I am pleased to share that households may apply for the new improvement items under the EASE programme from 1 April 2024.

speaker: The Minister of State for National Development (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: Households that have tapped on EASE in the past may apply again for the new items.

speaker: The Minister of State for National Development (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: The EASE programme is heavily subsidised by the Government.

speaker: The Minister of State for National Development (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: Today, under EASE, a Singaporean household living in a 3-room flat only pays 5% of the costs of the upgrades, with the rest covered by the Government.

speaker: The Minister of State for National Development (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: The new features under EASE 2.0 will adopt this same subsidy structure.

speaker: The Minister of State for National Development (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: A 3-room flat owner tapping on the full EASE programme, which includes a wheelchair lifter and the new EASE 2.0 features, can expect to pay only around $570, with the remaining cost of around $10,000 borne by the Government.

speaker: The Minister of State for National Development (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: Fuller details on the costs will be provided on HDB InfoWEB from 1 April this year.

speaker: The Minister of State for National Development (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: Mr Ong Hua Han had asked if we would provide financial support to persons with disabilities, or PwDs, to improve the accessibility of their HDB flats.

speaker: The Minister of State for National Development (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: As with EASE, non-elderly families with extenuating circumstances, such as households with PwDs, can apply for the new EASE 2.0 features on a case-by-case basis.

speaker: The Minister of State for National Development (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: With these new features under the EASE programme, we hope to assure our seniors and your loved ones that your homes will continue to be enhanced to meet your changing needs.

speaker: The Minister of State for National Development (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: In our interactions with young couples, we have heard that many are very keen to book a flat and settle down earlier.

speaker: The Minister of State for National Development (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: This includes those who are still studying full-time, undergoing National Service or those who have just completed their studies or National Service last year.

speaker: The Minister of State for National Development (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: Such couples do not qualify for the Enhanced CPF Housing Grant (EHG), which requires 12 months of continuous employment.

speaker: The Minister of State for National Development (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: We would like to continue supporting this group of young couples who are currently eligible for deferred income assessment and Staggered Downpayment Scheme (SDS).

speaker: The Minister of State for National Development (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: We hope this will help more young couples to move forward with their marriage and parenthood plans earlier.

speaker: The Minister of State for National Development (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: The second group of couples that we heard from through our engagements are those who have booked their BTO flat but need temporary accommodation while awaiting the completion of their new flat.

speaker: The Minister of State for National Development (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: Today, we provide subsidised temporary housing for these families who are waiting for their flat to be completed, under the Parenthood Provisional Housing Scheme (PPHS).

speaker: The Minister of State for National Development (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: Meanwhile, to support more families that qualify for PPHS, we will introduce the PPHS (Open Market) Voucher to help those renting HDB flats or bedrooms in the open market.

speaker: The Minister of State for National Development (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: Each eligible family will receive $300 a month and the payment is on a reimbursement basis.

speaker: The Minister of State for National Development (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: This PPHS voucher will provide some financial assistance for young families who rent a home while waiting for their BTO flat.

speaker: The Minister of State for National Development (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: For low-income families who are not ready to own a home and have no other housing options, we provide public rental housing to ensure that they have a safe and stable home.

speaker: The Minister of State for National Development (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: Over the past decade, about 8,300 public rental households have progressed to home ownership.

speaker: The Minister of State for National Development (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: From this group, nearly 950 have done so in 2023, the highest in the last five years.

speaker: The Minister of State for National Development (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: We hope that more public rental households will progress to home ownership in the coming year.

speaker: The Minister of State for National Development (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: We encourage these households to contact HDB if they need any help in the course of their home ownership journey.

speaker: The Minister of State for National Development (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: As our population ages, one of our key priorities is to ensure that seniors continue to live safely in their homes and age healthily within the community.

speaker: The Minister of State for National Development (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: We will do so through key initiatives under Age Well SG.

speaker: The Minister of State for National Development (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: First, we will expand the provision of the wireless Alert Alarm System (AAS) to all seniors aged 60 and above living in public rental flats.

speaker: The Minister of State for National Development (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: The wireless AAS is linked to nearby Active Ageing Centres and also CareLine, a 24/7 helpline that provides response to callers in distress.

speaker: The Minister of State for National Development (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: We will start implementing the wireless AAS expansion from January 2025.

speaker: The Minister of State for National Development (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: Next, we will expand the range of senior-friendly features offered under the Enhancement for Active Seniors programme (EASE), for all seniors.

speaker: The Minister of State for National Development (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: From 1 April 2024, seniors can choose to have lowered bathroom entrance kerbs, foldable grab bars and bidet sprays under EASE 2.0.

speaker: The Minister of State for National Development (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: This is on top of the features announced earlier such as the widening of bathroom entrances and folding shower chairs.

speaker: The Minister of State for National Development (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: The cost of these features will be heavily subsidised by the Government, at the same rate as it is now.

speaker: The Minister of State for National Development (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: In addition, I am pleased to share that households that have tapped on EASE in the past can reapply for the new features.

speaker: The Minister of State for National Development (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: This will benefit more than 100,000 additional flats, comprising older flats built up to 1999.

speaker: The Minister of State for National Development (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: Residents can look forward to therapeutic gardens with wheelchair-friendly planter boxes and barrier-free walkways that link to senior-centric facilities.

speaker: The Minister of State for National Development (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: With the expansion of wireless AAS for public rental flats as well as the launch of EASE 2.0 and the fifth phase of the NRP, we hope that seniors will feel safer living at home and ageing within the community. : To conclude, let me reaffirm our commitment to building an inclusive home for all Singaporeans.

speaker: The Minister of State for National Development (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: We will continue to build a home that responds to the diverse and evolving needs of our population, a home that integrates housing with social support to empower and uplift our lower-income households and a home that allows our seniors to age gracefully and safely within the community, in our neighbourhoods and homes.

speaker: Miss Cheryl Chan Wei Ling
text: I am actually happy to hear that the Government will be providing support through the enhanced Staggered Downpayment Scheme, or SDS, to help young couples pay for the downpayment of flats.

speaker: Miss Cheryl Chan Wei Ling
text: However, if you want to bring assurance to the young couples, I think it needs to go beyond just financial support.

speaker: Miss Cheryl Chan Wei Ling
text: So, if they needed more comprehensive support, can Minister share with us what are some ways that this can be done so that we can also address the problem around the falling TFR?

speaker: Miss Cheryl Chan Wei Ling
text: The second clarification I have is for Senior Minister of State Sim Ann.

speaker: Miss Cheryl Chan Wei Ling
text: In my cut, I asked about the MSO's Love Our 'Hood initiatives and also the fund that has been in place.

speaker: Miss Cheryl Chan Wei Ling
text: I think the Senior Minister of State was probably tight on time just now, so you did not mention very much about some of the initiatives that have resulted in tangible impact in other neighbourhoods in your reply.

speaker: Miss Cheryl Chan Wei Ling
text: I think having some insights to this will help others see how we can tap upon it and expand it across the island.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: But we have to see the enhanced Staggered Downpayment Scheme in light of a whole range of measures that we have put in place to help young families, specifically, but also Singaporeans generally, get access to their first home.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: The first, of course, is the ramp-up in housing supply.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: We make more flats available so that young couples who are looking for a flat in a location, not just in a Non-Mature Estate, but also in a Mature Estate, because they are looking to live nearer to their parents, nearer to their families, can find options.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: So, you are starting to see more BTO launches in more Mature Estates or in more central locations.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: That means you meet this year's demand through your launches, but you start building some to be launched the next year.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: So, when next year comes, there will be a number of flats which have waiting time of below three years, two years plus.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: And actually, a lot of young couples say that is about right for them.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: We were ramping that up, but COVID-19 hit; and we are going back on track.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: That voice came out very strongly and there was a lot of agreement in all our Forward Singapore Housing Conversations that we should really support this group.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: Then, in addition to the priority, we even allocate priority to new flats under the Family and Parenthood Priority Scheme (FPPS).

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: You will recall last year when we introduced the First-Timer (Parents and Married Couples), we also rejigged the Parenthood Priority Scheme to a Family and Parenthood Priority Scheme, so those first timers buying their very first home will be given first priority if applying for flats in Non-Mature Estates.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: Last year we increased the CPF Housing Grants to help lower- and middle-income households trying to buy resale flats.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: Some young couples want to buy resale flats near to their parents.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: And, of course, temporary housing through the PPHS supply to help the lower- and lower-middle income young couples who are trying to set up family, waiting for their flats, a place to stay in the meantime.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: So, we have to see the enhanced Staggered Downpayment Scheme in light of all these changes we have made, to continue to support young Singaporeans who want to settle down, buy their first home and start a family.

speaker: Ms Sim Ann
text: In response to Miss Cheryl Chan's clarification, indeed the MSO has been adopting a variety of methods to undertake community education.

speaker: Ms Sim Ann
text: The Love Our 'Hood initiative has one example that Members might recall, and it is us working with the volunteers and grassroots leaders from Mountbatten.

speaker: Ms Sim Ann
text: And when the initiative was reported in the media, it also got some attention from other communities that were inspired and wanted to do similar activities.

speaker: Ms Sim Ann
text: What the MSO has done is to share this playbook with other neighbourhoods that have similar illegal parking issues such as Bukit Gombak and Nee Soon South, and those that are interested can then take a leaf from this experience.

speaker: Ms Sim Ann
text: We also do community education in other ways.

speaker: Ms Sim Ann
text: So, this has also been helpful because the visitors have given us very useful feedback and they thought that this hands-on method is very good for internalising pro-social norms.

speaker: Ms Sim Ann
text: In fact, we had very good feedback from young people and children.

speaker: Ms Sim Ann
text: We have included a wide variety of stakeholders.

speaker: Ms Sim Ann
text: This includes cultural experts, includes representatives from religious organisations, from the media, from community volunteers, as well as even supermarkets that sell joss paper and related offerings.

speaker: Ms Sim Ann
text: I think this method of leveraging cultural awareness and knowledge, and getting the information to the people who are making decisions that could have downstream implications on their neighbours, I think that has also given us insights which we can apply to other areas and other municipal issues.

speaker: The Chairman
text: I counted, on hand, at least 12 Members who want to ask clarifications.

speaker: The Chairman
text: So, it is impossible to meet everyone's request.

speaker: The Chairman
text: So, again, my request, the same one: clarification short, and likewise, responses short.

speaker: Ms Hazel Poa
text: On the matter of the Shorter Waiting Time flats, I have acknowledged that the Government is building about 2,000 to 3,000 a year in my speech.

speaker: Ms Hazel Poa
text: I think my question is, because that forms only about 10% to 15% of the annual supply, why can it not be increased further to maybe about 50% of the supply?

speaker: Ms Hazel Poa
text: But I think the question here is, why do we say if there is no increase in supply?

speaker: Ms Hazel Poa
text: Actually, PSP did ask for ramping up the supply at the public housing debate in February of last year.

speaker: Ms Hazel Poa
text: So, can the Minister clarify why is it that there cannot be a further ramping up of supply?

speaker: Ms Hazel Poa
text: Mr Desmond Lee: It is a very broad question, so I take heed Chairman's request to keep it short.

speaker: Ms Hazel Poa
text: You launch in a given year, you want to make sure that you are able to meet demand.

speaker: Ms Hazel Poa
text: We have been able to bring BTO application rates down from a peak during COVID-19, to somewhere around pre-COVID-19 levels.

speaker: Ms Hazel Poa
text: But you do that and then also start building some in the year X to be launched in year X+1, that means, the next year, and you would have constructed a year or a year plus.

speaker: Ms Hazel Poa
text: That allows applicants who book a flat to be able to collect keys in two years-plus; in under three years or three years or less.

speaker: Ms Hazel Poa
text: When the sites get more infilled as you take more difficult sites, a lot more preparatory work has to come in; not to mention actual construction time: if you build on slopes, if the land is odd shape, if the geology requires extra piling and so on.

speaker: Ms Hazel Poa
text: The other question that the Member asked is why can we not ramp up supply and that was what PSP has called, that is, ramp up supply generally, build a lot more than 100,000, build a lot more Millennial Apartments.

speaker: Ms Hazel Poa
text: In fact, do not build Prime and Plus flats.

speaker: Ms Hazel Poa
text: Take all the Mature Estates, central estates, central location, just build rental flats for millennials for three to five years.

speaker: Ms Hazel Poa
text: And why not lower the age ceiling for singles?

speaker: Ms Hazel Poa
text: Why not you ramp up the 3-room, and I am quite sure there will be many other requests that she will make in the course of the coming years to basically provide supply for every constituency of Singaporeans that feel that they want more support.

speaker: Ms Hazel Poa
text: And as I have said many times, if land and resource were no constraint, we would certainly, as a responsible Government, want to meet genuine needs and there are needs on the ground, needs that Mr Louis Ng talked about, single parents and so on.

speaker: Ms Hazel Poa
text: And we meet most on those fronts, too.

speaker: Ms Hazel Poa
text: Every group is subject to some form of cap, whether it is an age ceiling, whether it is an income cap, whether it is a nationality requirement, household requirement; first timer, second timer versus Nth timer.

speaker: Ms Hazel Poa
text: All these ensure that, with limited land and resources, you are able to cater to the broad masses of Singaporeans and different categories.

speaker: Ms Hazel Poa
text: And over the years, we have been able to make some adjustments over time to allow more access.

speaker: Ms Hazel Poa
text: And that is for BTO flats which are a supply of flats in addition to the overall resale market supply that is available out there.

speaker: Ms Hazel Poa
text: And we are an island city-state, as Minister Indranee has said, with 730+ square kilometres, one of the most densely populated sovereign city-states in the world, the only island city-state in the world, and that means, unlike other cities, we do not just have to cater to housing and other amenities that city dwellers need; everything that the fully functioning sovereign state needs has to be within the city.

speaker: Ms Hazel Poa
text: And if you go to other cities that are like Singapore, you will find that actually the airport is far, far away; its port is far away; the crematorium is far away; the recycling plants are far away.

speaker: Ms Hazel Poa
text: All the undesirable necessities of city life, sometimes, in bigger countries can be parked outside the city.

speaker: Ms Hazel Poa
text: Ours is the karma of an island city-state, and I hope that all Members here will be able to take this back to your constituencies to share as part of the building of our knowledge and DNA of Singaporeans, to know that, for us, it will always be the need to balance severe trade-offs and make the best of our limited land and resources.

speaker: Ms Hazel Poa
text: And for a city-state like ours to have 80% living in national housing and 90% of them owning their homes and you compare that to larger countries with severe housing shortages, even coming to Singapore to study what we do, and we share, I think we must accept that we have, as a result of years of discipline, done well.

speaker: Ms Hazel Poa
text: If you want to find land to build, we have ample land.

speaker: Ms Hazel Poa
text: But land of the past, large green field sites, those are scarcer.

speaker: Ms Hazel Poa
text: We will have to make do with infill sites, we have to recycle the land, we have to rejuvenate, we have to work on brownfield sites, some of which have historical value.

speaker: Ms Hazel Poa
text: All these mean that land will become available to us in time and space.

speaker: Ms Hazel Poa
text: So, there may be a site that you have zoned for housing.

speaker: Ms Hazel Poa
text: Someone else is using that land in the meantime.

speaker: Mr Chong Kee Hiong
text: For Minister Desmond Lee, can I have your views on intensification of land use and the Integrated Hub for Bishan to free up more land and also to improve connectivity and accessibility?

speaker: Mr Chong Kee Hiong
text: The second clarification is that there have been several announcements on the redevelopment of brownfield, which the Minister mentioned again, such as Kranji Turf Club and Bukit Timah Turf City in the past year.

speaker: Mr Chong Kee Hiong
text: So, why is the Government redeveloping Gillman Barracks, which is another brownfield site?

speaker: Mr Chong Kee Hiong
text: What new recreational options can Singaporeans expect under the recreation master plan?

speaker: Mr Chong Kee Hiong
text: Are recreational options limited to activities that do not take up large tracks of land?

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: And intensification is a strategy within the broader strategy of disciplined long-term planning, and Minister Indranee talked about the long-term plan review, plan every 10 years for a 50-year horizon.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: And then, every five years, plan for a 10- to 15-year horizon and look at the little coloured dots on the master plan and look at the numbers that go with it.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: And so, intensification allows us, within limits of liveability, to make better use of our land.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: And, in fact, there is even a three-plus-one depot for three MRT lines converging and one bus depot all in, saving you lots and lots of land for other uses.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: We also better exploit the underground, so the underground master plan has been around for a number of years.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: And for those of you who have been to the Jurong Rock Cavern, you know that it is a feat of engineering which allows us to free up valuable land on the surface for more important economic uses and use the underground caverns for storage of condensates.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: Over and on top of that, we have the big moves, for example, the mention of "Long Island", which is many decades down the road.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: We have to start working on it now to provide a buffer against rising sea levels, more freshwater capacity, but also to create a lot of new land for future generations to exploit opportunities.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: And, of course, Paya Lebar Air Base and the greater Southern Waterfront through moving out our ports.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: All these also create space and room for Singaporeans to live out our dreams.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: As I said earlier, our aspirations are growing, our needs are also growing.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: With a fast-ageing population, there are both specific housing needs as well as amenities relating to ageing.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: And as our families' aspirations grow, you start to see fewer 3-Gen families, more nuclear households, more reconstituted households, more singles living on their own and a desire for greater space both within their homes, but also around the estate.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: And the greater desire for higher order needs of life.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: And so, we will need to open up sites, including in Gillman Barracks, because these allow us to build homes for Singaporeans, closer to their parents, closer to their workplaces and closer to desirable parks and other amenities for Singaporeans.

speaker: The Chairman
text: Sorry, I saw you raising your hand earlier.

speaker: The Chairman
text: Sorry Mr Kwek, I forgot to ask Second Minister Indranee for the second part of the reply.

speaker: The Chairman
text: I was eager to get as many supplementary questions put in.

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: I will try to keep it as brief as possible.

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: It follows on actually to what Minister Desmond Lee said because the previous clarifications were all asking Minister Desmond Lee how can we have more and more buildings on this 734 hectare.

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: But at the same time, in our conversations and as highlighted by Mr Chong, Singaporeans are also asking for more and more space, more recreational spaces, play spaces, places to breathe, places to walk.

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: So, that is where the recreational master plan comes in.

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: And that is where our agencies have actually been very creative.

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: It is a one-stop community hub and residents can access lifestyle and recreational amenities, such as eateries, shops, outdoor facilities and so on.

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: But another is PUB's collaboration with URA and NParks to have the PUB Active, Beautiful, Clean Waters (ABC Waters).

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: That strings out the spaces, so that you do not concentrate it in one.

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: So, going forward, the recreation master plan will focus on a variety of ways.

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: They will look at curating a variety of recreational nodes and trails island-wide.

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: They will also look at weaving play into our everyday spaces as well as involving the community in shaping recreational spaces.

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: So, I encourage everybody to participate with their ideas and feedback.

speaker: Mr Kwek Hian Chuan Henry
text: Chairperson, I would like to ask Minister of State Faishal Ibrahim a clarification about EASE.

speaker: Mr Kwek Hian Chuan Henry
text: First of all, I want to thank the Minister of State for sharing the good news on EASE 2.0, especially the fact that previous applicants can reapply.

speaker: Mr Kwek Hian Chuan Henry
text: So, can MND share how many seniors have benefited from EASE 1.0 in the past?

speaker: Mr Kwek Hian Chuan Henry
text: This number will help us understand potentially how many people would need 2.0 and then we can track the pace in which it rolls out to see whether any further push to get as many people to benefit this scheme is needed.

speaker: Mr Gerald Giam Yean Song
text: So, these enhancements do not actually reduce the price of the flat for young couples.

speaker: Mr Gerald Giam Yean Song
text: So, has the Minister considered that these changes might actually result in more couples being unable to make the larger ballooned payments before key collection and then they will incur the penalties like losing the initial downpayment and being debarred for the one year before they can reapply for subsidised housing?

speaker: Mr Gerald Giam Yean Song
text: To Senior Minister of State Sim Ann, can I confirm that the Senior Minister of State said that the replacement of the lift components I mentioned in my cut, the ARG, the main controller PCB, EBOPs and UPS can be expensed from the Lift Replacement Fund for existing lifts?

speaker: Mr Gerald Giam Yean Song
text: Can MND publish an exhaustive list of lift components which can be paid for using the Lift Replacement Fund so that it is clear to all Town Councils?

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: That is already reduced, compared to other people who would pay 10% and 20% respectively.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: For a group of young people, when we do a housing conversation, they approach us, they tell us their situation.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: These are young people who are ready to settle down and they say, "Well, flats take a few years, but we are ready to settle down.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: We are getting older and we want to start a family." When they apply while they are studying, let us, say, in tertiary, for example, in polytechnic, ITE, university and they are about to graduate in a year or two and maybe one of their partners is doing NS or they have already both completed their studies or completed NS, they have not yet chalked up enough of a track record to assess their eligibility for grant and loan.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: They say, "Yes, we can book but it is difficult, even with the Staggered Downpayment Scheme, to stump up the 5% or 10% respectively because we are not eligible for a grant or loan at that point in time." So, we say, for them, "Well, we will give you a deferred income assessment, that means, for your grant, it is not that you will get zero, you will get the grant, but we will assess it when you collect your keys." That has been helpful.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: We assess your loan eligibility when you collect your key.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: That is helpful because, by that time, they would have started working, maybe worked for one, two, three years, collect keys.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: But they want to book earlier and they are committed to settling down because they have known each other for a while.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: So, what we have done is do those things that I have responded to Miss Cheryl Chan on, priorities and all that.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: But when it comes to this particular kind of a micro issue that they face, but to them it is a big issue, we say, "Well, we will reduce the downpayment even further because we know your grant eligibility will come later." But to the Member's point that they will then have to pay up the rest anyway, it is true.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: But at that point in time, they would have worked, they would have accrued savings and CPF.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: They would have gotten the EHG if they are eligible as well as an HDB loan.

text: And the LRF can also be used for capital items, such as automatic rescue device and the main controller PCB, which Mr Gerald Giam has mentioned, which are not listed in the cyclical maintenance work schedule.
